change: the price check counted a student's progress as a denominator, so fourteen of its seventeen rows were healthy work
_context: Measured on production 2026-09-08, after the six real hits were fixed: every
remaining row was a false positive. The clearest is ap-csp bi-1 collaboration
quiz, which appeared THREE times on one healthy column, observed 1 and 3 and 5,
because three students answered 1, 3 and 5 of its 6 questions and stopped.
The check compared the authored price against each student's own summed
max_points. That is a denominator only where a page reports its whole run in
one row under the reserved 'score' item. Where a page reports one row per
question, the sum is how far the student got.
An alarm whose every row is healthy work is one people learn to skip, which is
the failure the reporter block next door was rewritten to avoid. The risk in
fixing it is the opposite one: two exclusions added to quiet an alarm is how an
alarm ends up never firing at all. Mutation three is aimed at exactly that.

checks._why: One student who abandoned a carrier page halfway would make a correct price look wrong. Different class from the one above, so it gets its own case.
checks.find: PARTITION BY course, unit, lesson, activity_type

checks.expect_failure: one abandoned run does not make a correct price look wrong

checks.name: count every student, not only those who were served the maximum
checks._why: The count is what a reader uses to judge how much of a class a row speaks for. Counting a student who abandoned the page as one who was served the full total overstates it.
checks.expect_failure: and how many students recorded that total

checks.name: the alarm silenced altogether, which is what two new exclusions risk
checks._why: Quieting a noisy check is one edit away from a check that never fires. The suite must go red when the REAL mispricing stops being reported, or these exclusions are unfalsifiable.
